target: Dia bilang dia akan datang sedikit terlambat.
english: He said he will come a little late.
grammar: bilang is the everyday 'say/tell': Dia bilang dia sibuk. = He said he's busy.

target: Ibu bilang makan malam sudah siap di meja.
english: Mom said dinner is already ready on the table.

target: Ayah bilang kita berangkat jam tujuh besok pagi.
english: Dad said we leave at seven tomorrow morning.

target: Manajer bilang rapat dimulai jam sepuluh pagi.
english: The manager said the meeting starts at ten in the morning.

target: Teman saya bilang restoran itu enak dan murah.
english: My friend said that restaurant is tasty and cheap.

target: Dia bilang kunci kamar ada di tasnya.
english: She said the room key is in her bag.

target: Petugas bilang kereta berikutnya datang jam sebelas.
english: The officer said the next train comes at eleven.

target: Adik saya bilang dia mau ikut ke pasar.
english: My little sibling said he wants to come along to the market.

target: Dokter bilang saya perlu minum lebih banyak air.
english: The doctor said I need to drink more water.

target: Dia bilang filmnya bagus, tapi terlalu panjang.
english: He said the movie is good, but too long.

target: Kakak bilang dia sudah membeli tiket untuk kita.
english: My older sibling said she already bought tickets for us.

target: Tetangga bilang cuaca akan panas sekali minggu ini.
english: The neighbor said the weather will be very hot this week.

target: Bos saya bilang laporan ini harus selesai hari Jumat.
english: My boss said this report must be finished on Friday.

target: Dia bilang toko itu tutup setiap hari Minggu.
english: He said that shop is closed every Sunday.

target: Sopir bilang jalan ke bandara sedang macet.
english: The driver said the road to the airport is congested right now.

target: Mereka bilang pantai di sana bersih dan tenang.
english: They said the beach over there is clean and calm.

target: Guru bilang anak saya rajin sekali di kelas.
english: The teacher said my child is very diligent in class.

target: Dia bilang harganya sudah termasuk sarapan.
english: He said the price already includes breakfast.

target: Kata siapa? Saya tidak pernah bilang begitu.
english: Says who? I never said that.
grammar: kata + person = 'X says': Kata siapa? = Says who? Kata ibu, boleh. = Mom says it's allowed.

target: Dia bilang ke saya dia tidak bisa datang malam ini.
english: He told me he can't come tonight.
grammar: bilang ke X = tell X: Dia bilang ke saya. = He told me.

target: Manajer bilang bahwa jadwal rapat berubah lagi.
english: The manager said that the meeting schedule changed again.
grammar: bahwa = 'that' is written-style; speakers usually drop it: Dia bilang (bahwa) dia setuju.

target: Dia bilang bahwa dia sudah membaca email saya.
english: He said that he had already read my email.

target: Petugas bilang bahwa penerbangan kami ditunda dua jam.
english: The officer said that our flight is delayed two hours.

target: Ibu bilang bahwa nenek akan menginap di rumah kita.
english: Mom said that grandma will stay over at our house.

target: Dia bilang bahwa kabar itu belum tentu benar.
english: She said that that news is not necessarily true.
grammar: belum tentu = not necessarily: Katanya begitu, tapi belum tentu benar.

target: Dalam suratnya, dia bilang bahwa dia ingin cepat pulang.
english: In his letter, he said that he wants to come home soon.

target: Dia hanya bilang dia lelah, tidak bilang kenapa.
english: He only said he was tired, he didn't say why.

target: Saya sudah bilang berkali-kali bahwa pintunya harus dikunci.
english: I have said many times that the door must be locked.

target: Tolong bilang ke ayah bahwa saya pulang agak malam.
english: Please tell dad that I'm coming home a bit late.
grammar: tolong bilang ke X = please tell X: Tolong bilang ke ibu, ya.

target: Tolong bilang ke sopir supaya menunggu di depan hotel.
english: Please tell the driver to wait in front of the hotel.
grammar: bilang supaya + verb = tell someone to do it: Bilang supaya dia menunggu.

target: Tolong bilang ke ibu kalau nasi di dapur sudah habis.
english: Please tell mom that the rice in the kitchen is finished.
grammar: After bilang, spoken Indonesian often uses kalau for 'that': Dia bilang kalau macet.

target: Tolong bilang ke tim bahwa rapat sore ini dibatalkan.
english: Please tell the team that this afternoon's meeting is canceled.

target: Tolong sampaikan salam saya ke keluarga kamu di Bandung.
english: Please pass on my greetings to your family in Bandung.
grammar: sampaikan salam = pass on greetings: Sampaikan salam saya ke ibu kamu.

target: Tolong sampaikan pesan ini ke manajer sebelum jam dua.
english: Please pass this message to the manager before two o'clock.

target: Jangan bilang ke siapa-siapa dulu, ini masih rahasia.
english: Don't tell anyone yet, this is still a secret.
grammar: siapa-siapa after a negative = anyone: Jangan bilang ke siapa-siapa.

target: Kalau kamu bertemu dia, tolong bilang saya menunggu di sini.
english: If you meet him, please tell him I'm waiting here.

target: Tolong bilang ke tamu bahwa kamarnya sudah siap.
english: Please tell the guest that their room is ready.

target: Bilang ke adikmu, makan siangnya ada di kulkas.
english: Tell your little sibling, his lunch is in the fridge.

target: Nanti saya bilang ke resepsionis soal AC yang rusak itu.
english: Later I'll tell the receptionist about the broken air conditioner.

target: Dia sudah bilang ke saya soal rencana liburan kalian.
english: He already told me about your vacation plans.

target: Katanya besok akan hujan deras sepanjang hari.
english: They say tomorrow it will rain heavily all day long.
grammar: katanya = 'they say / (s)he said' — a one-word rumor marker: Katanya besok libur.

target: Katanya restoran baru itu selalu ramai malam hari.
english: They say that new restaurant is always crowded at night.

target: Katanya dia pindah ke Surabaya bulan depan.
english: They say he's moving to Surabaya next month.

target: Katanya tiket konser itu sudah habis terjual.
english: They say the concert tickets are already sold out.

target: Katanya museum ini gratis setiap hari Kamis.
english: They say this museum is free every Thursday.

target: Katanya bos akan memberi tugas baru minggu depan.
english: They say the boss will give out new assignments next week.

target: Katanya jalan itu ditutup karena ada perbaikan.
english: They say that road is closed because there are repairs.

target: Katanya keluarga mereka sudah tinggal di sini sejak dulu.
english: They say their family has lived here since long ago.
grammar: sejak dulu = since long ago: Mereka di sini sejak dulu. = They've been here forever.

target: Katanya dia berhenti kerja karena mau membuka usaha sendiri.
english: They say he quit his job because he wants to open his own business.

target: Katanya hotel itu penuh sampai akhir bulan ini.
english: They say that hotel is full until the end of this month.

target: Katanya kopi di warung itu paling enak di kota ini.
english: They say the coffee at that stall is the tastiest in this city.

target: Katanya dia sakit, makanya dia tidak masuk hari ini.
english: They say he's sick, that's why he didn't come in today.

target: Katanya ada pasar malam di dekat stasiun minggu ini.
english: They say there's a night market near the station this week.

target: Saya belum yakin, tapi katanya harga bensin naik lagi.
english: I'm not sure yet, but they say the price of gasoline is going up again.

target: Katanya paman akan datang membawa oleh-oleh dari Bali.
english: They say uncle will come bringing souvenirs from Bali.

target: Menurut saya, warna biru lebih cocok untuk kamu.
english: In my opinion, the color blue suits you better.
grammar: menurut saya = in my opinion: Menurut saya, itu ide bagus.

target: Menurut dia, film itu terlalu sedih untuk anak-anak.
english: According to him, that movie is too sad for children.

target: Menurut dokter, ayah tidak boleh makan terlalu banyak gula.
english: According to the doctor, dad may not eat too much sugar.

target: Menurut berita, sore ini akan turun hujan deras.
english: According to the news, this afternoon heavy rain will fall.

target: Menurut peta ini, museumnya tidak jauh dari sini.
english: According to this map, the museum isn't far from here.
grammar: menurut also cites sources: menurut peta = according to the map.

target: Menurut ibu, masakan rumah lebih sehat daripada makanan restoran.
english: According to mom, home cooking is healthier than restaurant food.

target: Menurut kamu, baju yang mana yang paling bagus?
english: In your opinion, which shirt is the nicest?
grammar: Menurut kamu…? asks someone's opinion: Menurut kamu, yang mana lebih bagus?

target: Menurut mereka, kantor baru kita terlalu jauh dari stasiun.
english: According to them, our new office is too far from the station.

target: Menurut petugas, loket tiket dibuka jam delapan pagi.
english: According to the officer, the ticket counter opens at eight in the morning.

target: Menurut saya, rencana ini masih perlu dibahas lagi.
english: In my opinion, this plan still needs to be discussed again.

target: Menurut kakak, jalan kaki lebih cepat daripada naik mobil di sini.
english: According to my older sibling, walking is faster than taking a car here.

target: Menurut berita tadi pagi, jalan tol masih ditutup.
english: According to the news this morning, the toll road is still closed.

target: Menurut dia, kita sebaiknya berangkat lebih pagi besok.
english: According to her, we had better leave earlier tomorrow.
grammar: sebaiknya = it'd be better to: Sebaiknya kita pulang sekarang.

target: Menurut banyak orang, pegawai toko itu ramah dan sopan.
english: According to many people, the employees of that shop are friendly and polite.

target: Menurut ayah, harga mobil itu masih terlalu mahal.
english: According to dad, the price of that car is still too expensive.

target: Menurut teman kantor saya, kantin di lantai dua lebih murah.
english: According to my office friend, the canteen on the second floor is cheaper.

target: Menurut saya, kita tidak perlu buru-buru mengambil keputusan.
english: In my opinion, we don't need to rush into making a decision.

target: Menurut jadwal, bus terakhir berangkat jam sembilan malam.
english: According to the schedule, the last bus departs at nine at night.

target: Saya pikir kita harus mencoba restoran baru itu.
english: I think we have to try that new restaurant.
grammar: saya pikir = I think: Saya pikir dia benar. = I think he's right.

target: Saya rasa harga kamar ini terlalu mahal untuk kita.
english: I feel the price of this room is too expensive for us.
grammar: saya rasa = I feel / I'd say — a soft opinion: Saya rasa itu cukup.

target: Saya pikir dia sudah pulang, ternyata masih di kantor.
english: I thought he had gone home; it turns out he's still at the office.
grammar: saya pikir also = 'I thought (wrongly)': Saya pikir kamu sudah pulang.

target: Saya rasa kopi ini kurang manis untuk saya.
english: I feel this coffee isn't sweet enough for me.

target: Saya pikir rapat ini bisa selesai sebelum jam dua belas.
english: I think this meeting can finish before twelve o'clock.

target: Saya rasa dia tidak akan datang ke pesta malam ini.
english: I feel he won't come to the party tonight.

target: Saya pikir jalan kaki saja, soalnya hotelnya dekat.
english: I think let's just walk, since the hotel is close.
grammar: soalnya = everyday 'because': Kami di rumah, soalnya hujan.

target: Saya rasa kita pernah bertemu di suatu tempat sebelumnya.
english: I feel we have met somewhere before.
grammar: pernah = have ever / once: Saya pernah ke Bali. = I've been to Bali.

target: Saya pikir warna ini cocok dengan tasmu.
english: I think this color goes well with your bag.

target: Saya rasa ukuran baju ini terlalu kecil untuk ayah.
english: I feel the size of this shirt is too small for dad.

target: Saya pikir kamu benar soal masalah jadwal kemarin.
english: I think you're right about yesterday's schedule problem.

target: Saya rasa anak-anak sudah terlalu lelah untuk jalan-jalan lagi.
english: I feel the kids are already too tired to walk around any more.

target: Awalnya saya pikir ini mudah, ternyata cukup sulit.
english: At first I thought this was easy; it turns out it's quite hard.
grammar: ternyata = it turns out: Saya pikir mahal, ternyata murah.

target: Saya rasa lebih baik kita tanya orang di sana.
english: I feel it's better if we ask the person over there.

target: Saya pikir dia setuju, ternyata dia menolak rencana itu.
english: I thought he agreed; it turns out he rejected the plan.
grammar: menolak = to turn down: Dia menolak tawaran itu. = He turned down that offer.

target: Kamu pikir kita bisa sampai sebelum toko tutup?
english: Do you think we can get there before the shop closes?

target: Saya rasa porsi di sini cukup besar untuk dua orang.
english: I feel the portions here are big enough for two people.

target: Saya pikir begitu juga, kita memang perlu istirahat.
english: I think so too, we really do need a rest.

target: Saya setuju dengan ide itu, tapi waktunya kurang tepat.
english: I agree with that idea, but the timing isn't quite right.
grammar: setuju = agree; the opposite is simply tidak setuju: Saya tidak setuju.

target: Kami semua setuju rapatnya dipindah ke hari Rabu.
english: We all agree the meeting is moved to Wednesday.

target: Ibu tidak setuju kalau kamu pulang terlalu malam.
english: Mom doesn't agree with you coming home too late.

target: Apakah kamu setuju dengan pendapatnya tadi?
english: Do you agree with his opinion just now?
grammar: apakah opens a yes/no question: Apakah kamu setuju? = Do you agree?

target: Ayah setuju, tapi dia meminta kita hati-hati di jalan.
english: Dad agrees, but he asks us to be careful on the road.

target: Saya kurang setuju dengan rencana itu, terlalu berisiko.
english: I don't quite agree with that plan; it's too risky.
grammar: kurang softens a no: kurang setuju = don't quite agree, kurang suka = don't really like.

target: Mereka belum setuju soal harga sewa rumah itu.
english: They haven't agreed yet about the rent for that house.

target: Kalau semua setuju, kita berangkat hari Sabtu pagi.
english: If everyone agrees, we leave on Saturday morning.

target: Dia setuju membantu kita menyiapkan acara ulang tahun nenek.
english: She agrees to help us prepare grandma's birthday party.

target: Saya setuju sekali, tempat ini memang cocok untuk keluarga.
english: I totally agree, this place really is suitable for families.

target: Bos belum setuju dengan anggaran baru untuk proyek kita.
english: The boss hasn't agreed yet to the new budget for our project.

target: Kenapa kamu tidak setuju? Coba jelaskan alasanmu pelan-pelan.
english: Why don't you agree? Try to explain your reason slowly.

target: Akhirnya kami setuju untuk membayar biaya bensin bersama-sama.
english: In the end we agreed to pay the fuel costs together.

target: Suami saya sudah setuju, jadi kami akan membeli rumah itu.
english: My husband has agreed, so we are going to buy that house.

target: Dia tanya kapan kita datang ke rumahnya.
english: He asked when we're coming to his house.
grammar: tanya + question word reports a question: Dia tanya kapan kita datang.

target: Ibu tanya di mana kamu menyimpan kunci motornya.
english: Mom asked where you keep the motorbike's key.

target: Petugas tanya berapa lama kami akan tinggal di sini.
english: The officer asked how long we will stay here.
grammar: berapa lama = how long: Berapa lama kamu tinggal di sini?

target: Dia tanya apakah kamar ini masih kosong besok malam.
english: He asked whether this room is still vacant tomorrow night.
grammar: apakah mid-sentence = 'whether': Dia tanya apakah saya lapar.

target: Teman saya tanya siapa yang akan menjemput kita di bandara.
english: My friend asked who will pick us up at the airport.

target: Bos tanya kenapa laporan penjualan bulan lalu belum masuk.
english: The boss asked why last month's sales report hasn't come in yet.

target: Saya tidak tahu apakah dia jadi datang atau tidak.
english: I don't know whether he's actually coming or not.
grammar: jadi before a verb = 'actually end up': Jadi berangkat? = Still going?

target: Dia tidak bilang di mana kita akan bertemu besok.
english: He didn't say where we will meet tomorrow.

target: Tolong tanya ke petugas jam berapa loket ini dibuka.
english: Please ask the officer what time this counter opens.

target: Saya lupa menanyakan berapa harga tiket untuk anak-anak.
english: I forgot to ask how much tickets for children cost.
grammar: menanyakan X = to ask about X: menanyakan harga = to ask the price.

target: Kakak tanya apakah kamu mau ikut makan malam bersama.
english: My older sibling asked whether you want to join dinner together.

target: Dia ingin tahu bagaimana cara memesan taksi lewat aplikasi.
english: She wants to know how to order a taxi through the app.
grammar: bagaimana cara + verb = how to: Bagaimana cara memesan tiket?

target: Tamu itu tanya apakah harga kamar sudah termasuk sarapan.
english: That guest asked whether the room price already includes breakfast.

target: Anak saya terus tanya kapan kita pergi ke kebun binatang.
english: My child keeps asking when we're going to the zoo.

target: Dia tanya bagaimana rasanya tinggal jauh dari keluarga.
english: She asked what it feels like to live far from family.
grammar: rasanya = 'it feels / the taste of it': Bagaimana rasanya? = How is it?

target: Saya mau tanya dulu ke istri saya sebelum memutuskan.
english: I want to ask my wife first before deciding.

target: Mereka tanya kenapa kami pindah ke kota sekecil ini.
english: They asked why we moved to a town this small.

target: Dia belum menjawab pertanyaan saya tentang jadwal minggu depan.
english: He hasn't answered my question about next week's schedule yet.

target: Kalau tidak jelas, jangan malu bertanya sekali lagi.
english: If it's not clear, don't be embarrassed to ask one more time.
grammar: jangan malu = don't be shy: Jangan malu bertanya di kelas.

target: Sebelum pulang, dia sempat tanya kabar keluargamu.
english: Before going home, he found a moment to ask how your family is.
grammar: sempat = found a moment to: Saya sempat mampir tadi.
